EVIDENCE: eval/results.json (40 scenarios written by the author, one run at temperature 0 with seed 9; a second run gave 34 of 40, 0.85); the agent called the retrieval tool in 37 of the 40 scenarios and no other model tool (the date parser and the currency formatter are plain functions that the model cannot call); the 3,200 past claims are synthetic; the replay time is the median of 20 replays on one laptop; CI time is from the last 10 runs.
do_not_claim: a production model, a deployment or real users (it runs on one laptop and nothing was deployed)
a multi-tool agent or 'three tools' (the retrieval tool is the only tool the model can call)
0.875 as a stable figure (a single run; a second run gave 0.85)
accuracy on real claims (the claims are synthetic and the scenarios were written by the author)
any comparison with other models (one 8B model only)
tech_stack: Python, Ollama, SQLite, pytest, Docker

do_not_claim: clinical or patient-outcome impact (only form completion was measured)
'HIPAA compliance' (the form stored nothing itself, and another team owned the compliance review)
significance beyond what the dashboard reported (p = 0.03, with no correction for multiple tests)
tech_stack: React, TypeScript, Jest, Cypress, REST, Lighthouse

bullet: Reduced compaction time for a 6 GB dataset from 91 s to 29.5 s (3.08x speed-up) by merging four tables at a time instead of two.
facts: Cut the compaction of a 6 GB data set from 91 s to 29.5 s, a 3.08x speed-up, by merging 4 tables at a time instead of 2.
scope: ORIGIN: personal project, written to learn how storage engines recover from crashes. EVIDENCE: bench/results-2025-06.csv (one 8-core laptop with NVMe; one writer goroutine; median of 5 runs; the throughput gain is attributed to the larger write buffer by the flush counts, 910 down to 140); the recovery test replays a log of exactly 8,000 records; the 6 GB compaction input is synthetic; the crash test is test/crash_test.go (200 seeds, no acknowledged write lost, the model compared after every recovery); the follower test is test/follower_test.go (2,000 randomized reads).
do_not_claim: production use or real users (it has only run on one laptop and in CI)
multi-writer throughput (only one writer goroutine was benchmarked, and the gain came from the write buffer)
durability guarantees beyond the 200 tested crashes (power-loss behaviour of the disk was not tested)
read scaling or follower throughput (the follower's speed was never measured)
any comparison with other storage engines (none was run)
tech_stack: Go, Make, pprof, GitHub Actions
